quests.hint: Parking in a fire lane despite the clearly posted signs forbidding it.
quests.explanation: IN- shifts to IL- before a root starting with L. IN- + LEGAL = ILLEGAL, not legal, against the law.
quests.meaningBreakdown: IL (prefix, 'not,' n shifts to l before l) + LEGAL (root)
quests.instruction: IN- changes shape before certain letters. Which version fits LEGAL?

quests.hint: An argument that contradicts itself halfway through and no longer makes sense.
quests.explanation: ILLOGICAL is IN- + LOGICAL, with IN- shifting to IL- before L, meaning not based on sound reasoning.
quests.meaningBreakdown: IL (prefix, 'not') + LOGICAL (root)
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: A prescription scrawled so messily that the pharmacist can't make out the dosage.
quests.explanation: IL- + LEGIBLE = ILLEGIBLE, not able to be read. UN- doesn't attach to LEGIBLE in standard English — 'unlegible' isn't a real word, since LEGIBLE specifically takes IL-.
quests.meaningBreakdown: IL (prefix, 'not,' n shifts to l before l) + LEGIBLE (root)
quests.instruction: IN- changes shape before certain letters. Which version fits LEGIBLE?

quests.hint: A heartbeat that speeds up and slows down with no consistent pattern.
quests.explanation: IN- shifts to IR- before a root starting with R. IN- + REGULAR = IRREGULAR, not regular or consistent.
quests.meaningBreakdown: IR (prefix, 'not,' n shifts to r before r) + REGULAR (root)
quests.instruction: IN- changes shape before certain letters. Which version fits REGULAR?

quests.hint: A driver who speeds off after a fender bender without checking if anyone's hurt.
quests.explanation: IRRESPONSIBLE is IN- + RESPONSIBLE, with IN- shifting to IR- before R, meaning failing to act with proper care or duty.
quests.meaningBreakdown: IR (prefix, 'not') + RESPONSIBLE (root)
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: Bringing up an old childhood nickname in the middle of a serious business meeting.
quests.explanation: IR- + RELEVANT = IRRELEVANT, not relevant or connected to the matter at hand. NON- wouldn't fit here — RELEVANT specifically pairs with IR-, following the same doubling pattern as IRREGULAR.
quests.meaningBreakdown: IR (prefix, 'not,' n shifts to r before r) + RELEVANT (root)
quests.instruction: IN- changes shape before certain letters. Which version fits RELEVANT?

quests.hint: A 30-year-old who still throws a tantrum when he doesn't get his way.
quests.explanation: IN- shifts to IM- before M, giving IMMATURE — not mature. This is the same spelling-shift pattern you saw with IMPOSSIBLE, just triggered by a different starting letter.
quests.meaningBreakdown: IM (prefix, 'not,' n shifts to m before m) + MATURE (root)
quests.instruction: IN- changes shape before certain letters. Which version fits MATURE?

quests.hint: Someone who never learned to read or write growing up.
quests.explanation: ILLITERATE is IN- + LITERATE, with IN- shifting to IL- before L, meaning unable to read or write.
quests.meaningBreakdown: IL (prefix, 'not') + LITERATE (root)
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: Panicking and refusing to ever fly again after hearing about a single delayed flight.
quests.explanation: IN- shifts to IR- before R, giving IRRATIONAL — not rational, not based on logical thinking. Recognizing this whole family (IN-/IM-/IL-/IR-, all meaning 'not,' each shaped by the next letter) helps you handle unfamiliar words with confidence.
quests.meaningBreakdown: IR (prefix, 'not,' n shifts to r before r) + RATIONAL (root)
quests.instruction: IN- changes shape before certain letters. Which version fits RATIONAL?

quests.hint: A surprise birthday party that leaves the guest of honor grinning all night.
quests.explanation: -FUL means 'full of.' DELIGHT + -FUL = DELIGHTFUL, full of delight. -OUS also means 'full of,' but DELIGHT specifically pairs with -FUL, not -OUS.
quests.meaningBreakdown: DELIGHT (root) + FUL (suffix, 'full of')
quests.instruction: -FUL and -OUS both mean 'full of,' but pair with different roots. Which fits here?

quests.hint: A waiter who greets every table with a warm smile and patient manners.
quests.explanation: COURTEOUS comes from COURTESY plus -OUS (with a spelling shift), full of courtesy and good manners.
quests.meaningBreakdown: COURTE (root) + OUS (suffix, 'full of')
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: A host who welcomes every guest warmly, even the ones who show up unannounced.
quests.explanation: -OUS forms GRACIOUS from GRACE (with a spelling shift), full of grace and kindness. -FUL would sound unnatural here — GRACEFUL is a real word, but it describes elegant movement, a related yet distinct meaning from warm, welcoming manners.
quests.meaningBreakdown: GRACI (root) + OUS (suffix, 'full of')
quests.instruction: -FUL and -OUS both mean 'full of,' but pair with different roots. Which fits here?

quests.hint: Taking apart a bookshelf to move it, then putting all the pieces back together in the new apartment.
quests.explanation: RE- ('again') gives REASSEMBLE, to put something back together after taking it apart. UN- would instead mean simply taking it apart without rebuilding, and DIS- doesn't naturally attach to ASSEMBLE at all.
quests.meaningBreakdown: RE (prefix, 'again') + ASSEMBLE (root)
quests.instruction: RE-, UN-, and DIS- can look similar in negative contexts. Which fits this situation?

quests.hint: Loosening your collar by undoing the top fastener after a long day in a dress shirt.
quests.explanation: UN- + BUTTON = UNBUTTON, to undo something fastened. RE- would instead mean fastening it again, and DIS- doesn't naturally pair with BUTTON in this sense.
quests.meaningBreakdown: UN (prefix, reverses the action) + BUTTON (root)
quests.instruction: RE-, UN-, and DIS- can look similar in negative contexts. Which fits this situation?

quests.hint: A driver taking their foot off the clutch pedal to shift the car out of gear.
quests.explanation: DIS- + ENGAGE = DISENGAGE, to stop being connected or involved. UN- doesn't pair with ENGAGE in standard English — ENGAGE specifically takes DIS-.
quests.meaningBreakdown: DIS (prefix, reverses the connection) + ENGAGE (root)
quests.instruction: RE-, UN-, and DIS- can look similar in negative contexts. Which fits this situation?

quests.hint: The details a tour guide shares about a building's history and architecture.
quests.explanation: -ATION is a common spelling of -TION, often appearing after verbs ending in a silent E or a consonant cluster. INFORM + -ATION = INFORMATION, facts told or made known.
quests.meaningBreakdown: INFORM (root) + ATION (suffix, forms a noun of result)
quests.instruction: Which suffix fits the meaning below?

quests.hint: A clear, step-by-step answer for why the printer keeps jamming.
quests.explanation: EXPLANATION comes from EXPLAIN (with a spelling shift) plus -ATION, the act of making something clear.
quests.meaningBreakdown: EXPLAN (root) + ATION (suffix, forms a noun of result)
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: The creative power that lets a child build entire worlds out of cardboard boxes.
quests.explanation: -ATION forms IMAGINATION from IMAGINE (the E drops before the suffix), the ability to form new ideas mentally. -MENT wouldn't fit — 'imaginement' isn't a word, since IMAGINE specifically takes -ATION.
quests.meaningBreakdown: IMAGIN (root, e dropped) + ATION (suffix, forms a noun of result)
quests.instruction: Which suffix correctly completes this word?

quests.hint: The reason a fire alarm test is taken seriously by every employee in the building.
quests.explanation: -ANCE turns certain adjectives (often ending in -ANT) into abstract nouns. IMPORTANT becomes IMPORTANCE, the quality of mattering a great deal.
quests.meaningBreakdown: IMPORT (root) + ANCE (suffix, forms an abstract noun)
quests.instruction: Which suffix fits the meaning below?

quests.hint: A ballet dancer's flawless routine on opening night, met with a standing ovation.
quests.explanation: PERFORMANCE is PERFORM + -ANCE, the act of performing or how well something is carried out.
quests.meaningBreakdown: PERFORM (root) + ANCE (suffix, forms a noun of action)
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: The help a customer service rep gives you over the phone when your order goes wrong.
quests.explanation: -ANCE forms ASSISTANCE from ASSIST, the act of helping. -ENCE wouldn't fit here — 'assistence' isn't standard spelling, since ASSIST specifically takes -ANCE.
quests.meaningBreakdown: ASSIST (root) + ANCE (suffix, forms a noun of action)
quests.instruction: Which suffix correctly completes this word?

quests.hint: The simple fact that something is real and actually there, whether or not anyone notices it.
quests.explanation: -ENCE, closely related to -ANCE, also forms abstract nouns — often from adjectives ending in -ENT. EXIST becomes EXISTENCE, the state of being real.
quests.meaningBreakdown: EXIST (root) + ENCE (suffix, forms an abstract noun)
quests.instruction: -ANCE and -ENCE mean nearly the same thing, but each root has one correct spelling. Which fits here?

quests.hint: The steady calm a seasoned pilot feels while landing during turbulence.
quests.explanation: CONFIDENCE comes from CONFIDENT plus -ENCE, the quality of being self-assured.
quests.meaningBreakdown: CONFID (root) + ENCE (suffix, forms an abstract noun)
quests.instruction: Which word matches this situation?

quests.hint: What separates two nearly identical paintings, spotted only by a trained art expert.
quests.explanation: -ENCE forms DIFFERENCE from DIFFER, the quality of not being the same. -ANCE wouldn't fit — 'differance' isn't standard spelling, since DIFFER specifically takes -ENCE.
quests.meaningBreakdown: DIFFER (root) + ENCE (suffix, forms an abstract noun)
quests.instruction: -ANCE and -ENCE mean nearly the same thing, but each root has one correct spelling. Which fits here?

quests.hint: A school budget so tight it can't even cover basic supplies for every classroom.
quests.explanation: IN- + ADEQUATE = INADEQUATE, not enough or not sufficient. This reviews the IN-/IM-/IL-/IR- family: the base form IN- applies here because ADEQUATE starts with a vowel, not L, R, M, B, or P.
quests.meaningBreakdown: IN (prefix, 'not') + ADEQUATE (root)
quests.instruction: Review: which 'not' prefix fits a root starting with a vowel?

quests.hint: Assuming a task will take twenty minutes when it actually takes three hours.
quests.explanation: UNDER- + ESTIMATE = UNDERESTIMATE, to guess a lower amount than the true one. OVER- would describe the opposite mistake — guessing too high.
quests.meaningBreakdown: UNDER (prefix, 'too little') + ESTIMATE (root)
quests.instruction: Review: OVER- means 'too much.' UNDER- means 'too little.' Which fits here?

quests.hint: A camper who builds a working shelter out of nothing but branches and a poncho.
quests.explanation: -FUL forms RESOURCEFUL from RESOURCE, full of the skill to find clever solutions with whatever is available. Across this unit, -FUL and -OUS have both meant 'full of,' but each root commits to only one.
quests.meaningBreakdown: RESOURCE (root) + FUL (suffix, 'full of')
quests.instruction: Review: -FUL and -OUS both mean 'full of.' Which fits RESOURCE?

quests.hint: A fortune teller claiming to know exactly what will happen in your future.
quests.explanation: FORE- + TELL = FORETELL, to tell something before it happens. RE- would mean telling it again, and PRE- doesn't naturally attach to TELL — each of these 'before/again' prefixes has settled on its own set of words.
quests.meaningBreakdown: FORE (prefix, 'before') + TELL (root)
quests.instruction: Mastery check: RE- ('again'), PRE- ('before'), and FORE- ('before,' an older pattern) — which fits TELL?

quests.hint: The trait shared by two cousins who look so alike that strangers assume they're twins.
quests.explanation: -ITY forms SIMILARITY from SIMILAR, the quality of being alike. -ANCE and -ENCE build the same kind of abstract noun, but from a different set of roots (like IMPORTANCE and EXISTENCE) — three suffixes with one shared job, divided among different words.
quests.meaningBreakdown: SIMILAR (root) + ITY (suffix, forms an abstract noun)
quests.instruction: Mastery check: -ITY, -ANCE, and -ENCE all build abstract nouns. Which fits SIMILAR?

quests.hint: A come-from-behind win so unlikely that bettors never saw it coming.
quests.explanation: IN- shifts to IM- before P, giving IMPROBABLE — not probable, unlikely. After this whole unit on contrast and discrimination, the real goal isn't memorizing each word — it's recognizing the pattern well enough to handle a brand-new one like this with confidence.
quests.meaningBreakdown: IM (prefix, 'not,' n shifts to m before p) + PROBABLE (root)
quests.instruction: Mastery check: which version of 'not' fits a root starting with P?
